info.title: Ambivo Inventory API
info.description:
**Ambivo Inventory** tracks what stock exists, where it is, what it is worth, and
what to reorder. It runs inside the Ambivo Core API (`ingress.ambivo.com`) and
shares its auth, tenancy, access control and response envelope. There is no
separate Inventory service.

## Where stock lives: tenant → site → location → bin

Every balance is keyed on **(tenant, site, product, location, bin)**. The codes are
a hierarchy, not free text:

| Level | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `site_code` | The premises. Also an **ACL primitive**. | `dtcafe` |
| `location_code` | An area within the site. | `storage` |
| `bin_code` | The shelf. Optional. | `A3` |

⚠ `site_code` is an access-control code, not geography. It is part of the balance
key, so two different site codes are two different balances.

### The place registry

Locations and bins are registered under their site on the tenant document:

```
tenants.site_list[]                    a site
  .location_list[]                     {code, name, kind, is_active, bins_required, bin_list}
    .bin_list[]                        {code, name, is_active}
```

* A blank `location_code` is valid and means the site's **main area**. It never
  falls back to a product's `default_location_code`.
* A blank `bin_code` is valid unless the location has `bins_required: true`.
* Codes never change once created. A rename changes `name` only.
* Manage it with the place routes: `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` under
  `/user/site/{site_code}/location`. Pick from it with
  `GET /user/site/location/picklist` and `GET /user/site/bin/picklist`.
* Location and bin codes already on `inventory_item` rows are registered
  automatically, once per tenant (active, name = code), the first time the
  registry is read. A site registered later is backfilled the same way, once,
  the next time the registry is read. A blank site, or a tenant with no site registry, has nowhere
  to register a location. Stock moving there, in or out, is accepted only with a
  blank location and bin (the main area); a nonblank one is refused with
  `INVENTORY_LOCATION_UNKNOWN` or `INVENTORY_BIN_UNKNOWN`, unless stock is going
  out of a place where that product has stock (see below).

### Every stock write checks its place

Movements (a transfer checks the source AND the destination), write-downs, goods
receipts, count scopes and `POST /user/inventory_item` are refused before
anything is written when:

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_SITE_CODE_UNKNOWN` | the site is not registered (tenant has a site registry) |
| `INVENTORY_LOCATION_UNKNOWN` | a nonblank location is not registered at that site. Also when the site is blank or the tenant has no site registry |
| `INVENTORY_BIN_UNKNOWN` | a nonblank bin is not registered at that location (or the location is blank). Also when the site is blank or the tenant has no site registry |
| `INVENTORY_BIN_REQUIRED` | stock is going INTO a location with `bins_required` and the bin is blank (going out is allowed) |
| `INVENTORY_PLACE_INACTIVE` | stock is going INTO an inactive location or bin (going out is allowed) |

A count scope and a write-down check only that their codes are registered.
They are not checked at a blank site or in a tenant with no site registry. A
cost update checks only its `site_code`.

`POST /user/inventory_item` and `POST /user/inventory_count_session` resolve the
site first. On a tenant with no site registry, a nonblank `site_code` is refused
with `INVENTORY_SITE_CODE_UNKNOWN`. On a tenant with a registry, an unregistered
`site_code` is refused with `INVENTORY_SITE_CODE_UNKNOWN` too, and `data` is
`{"site_code": "..."}`.

The refusal carries the place in `data`:
`{"result": 2, "error_code": "INVENTORY_BIN_REQUIRED", "error": {"message": "..."},
"data": {"site_code": "dtcafe", "location_code": "racks", "bin_code": ""}}`.
A goods receipt carries the same codes and `data` from the procurement endpoint.
A write-down reports refusals per position; each refused entry carries the same
`data`.

Stock going OUT of an unregistered place is allowed when that product's stock
row at exactly that place is not empty. An unregistered place is one refused
with `INVENTORY_SITE_CODE_UNKNOWN`, `INVENTORY_LOCATION_UNKNOWN` or
`INVENTORY_BIN_UNKNOWN`. This includes a location or bin at a blank site or in
a tenant with no site registry. Empty means `qty_on_hand`, `qty_wip`, `qty_reserved`
and `qty_on_order` are all 0. The stock can then be moved or counted down. Stock going in
is still refused, except a `count` correction to a position that product already
has a balance row at.

"Going IN" is a receipt, a positive adjustment or count, a WIP receipt, a
transfer's destination, a goods receipt line and `POST /user/inventory_item`.

A transfer whose source and destination are the same place (codes compared
trimmed) is refused with `INVENTORY_TRANSFER_SAME_LOCATION`, carrying the place
in `data`.

## Running balance on every movement

Every `inventory_txn` written from 2026-09 carries the state of its position
(site + location + bin + product) immediately before and after it was applied.
Rows written earlier do not have them. Show nothing for them.

A running balance field with no value is not stored. List and detail reads
leave it out of the row. The `inventory_txn` object in a `POST /user/inventory_txn` answer carries
it as an empty string.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `qty_on_hand_before` / `qty_on_hand_after` | position on-hand, in the stocking `uom` |
| `unit_cost_before` / `unit_cost_after` | position unit cost |
| `value_before` / `value_after` | position stock value, in the row's currency |
| `balance_seq` | 1, 2, 3 ... per position, in apply order |

A **transfer** is one row and carries `from_*` and `to_*` variants of every field
(`from_qty_on_hand_before`, ..., `to_balance_seq`); its plain fields have no value.
A movement at one place has no value in its `from_*` and `to_*` fields.
A **write-down** moves value and unit cost, and its quantity before equals after.
A **count posting** has the variance as `qty`.

`qty_on_hand_after - qty_on_hand_before` equals the signed quantity moved. The
figures are computed from the balance at apply time, in the same write that moves
it. On a replica set (production) the balance row and the movement commit in one
MongoDB transaction. `GET /user/inventory/balance_check` lists positions whose
`balance_seq` has a gap.

## The entities

| Entity | What it is |
|---|---|
| `inventory_item` | A **balance**: one product at one place. Not the product. |
| `inventory_txn` | A **movement**. The only thing that changes a balance. |
| `inventory_count_session` | A **stocktake**, with lines. |
| `inventory_count_line` | One place and product on a stocktake. |
| `inventory_lot` | A lot or a serial number. |
| `inventory_forecast` | Projected vs actual consumption for one period. |

Called **inventory transactions**, never "ledger" — the general ledger belongs to
Ambivo Books, and conflating the two is how a stock question gets answered with an
accounting one.

## Two rules that shape the whole API

**`inventory_txn` has no PATCH and no DELETE route.** A correction is a new
offsetting movement.

**Nothing writes `qty_on_hand` directly.** A quantity changes by posting a movement
or posting a count. `PATCH /user/inventory_item/{id}` refuses a balance field with
`INVENTORY_BALANCE_NOT_WRITABLE`. `POST /user/inventory_item` refuses `qty_on_hand`
and `opening_qty` with `INVENTORY_OPENING_QTY_NOT_ALLOWED`.

## Units of measure

Every product carries a UoM from a fixed registry
(`GET /entity/data?entity_type=inventory_uom&action=picklist`).
Each unit has a dimension (`count`, `weight`, `volume`, `length`) and a precision.
Quantities are rounded to the product's precision, so `1.75 kg` stays `1.75`.

Item types are `discrete`, `measured`, `catch_weight`, `assembly` and
`non_stock` (`GET /entity/data?entity_type=inventory_item_type&action=picklist`). A `non_stock` item has no stock
rows; a movement for one is refused with `INVENTORY_ITEM_NOT_STOCKED`.

Pack units (`case`, `box`, `tray` and others) have no fixed size. The size comes
from the product's `uom_conversion_dict`, for example `{"case": 24}`. With no
entry the movement is refused with `INVENTORY_PACK_SIZE_UNKNOWN`. `dozen` is always 12.

⚠ **A unit cost is a rate.** It is stored to 6 decimal places, and only the
extended value is rounded to cents. When `uom` differs from the stocking unit,
the quantity and the unit cost are converted by the same factor.

## Response envelope

Success and refusals are HTTP **200** and carry the platform envelope. Branch on
`result`:

```json
{ "result": 1, "inventory_item": [ ... ], "total_count": 42, "page_num": 1, "page_size": 50 }
{ "result": 2, "error_code": "INVENTORY_UOM_UNKNOWN", "error": { "message": "..." } }
{ "result": 2, "error_code": "INVENTORY_PLACE_HAS_STOCK", "error": { "message": "..." },
  "data": { "site_code": "dtcafe", "location_code": "storage", "bin_code": "",
            "qty_on_hand": 12, "position_count": 2 } }
```

Two gates answer with another status. A request without a valid token gets HTTP
**401** with an empty body. A tenant whose account is not yet approved gets HTTP
**403** with `{"result": 2, "error_code": "Account Review Pending before this feature is enabled"}`.

A refusal that needs to say WHICH thing was refused puts those details in a
top-level `data` object beside `error_code`. Place refusals always carry
`site_code`, `location_code` and `bin_code` there.

The `/list` routes key their rows by entity name (`inventory_item`,
`inventory_txn`, `inventory_count_session`, `inventory_count_line`,
`inventory_forecast`, `inventory_lot`). Most report routes put their rows in a
`data` array. The lot reports use `lot_list` and the matrix routes use
`variant_list`. The site location and bin picklists use `location` and `bin`.
On a refusal, `data` is an object.

On the `/list` routes, `total_count` is the number of matching rows on page 1.
On every later page it is 0.

A read that fails answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`. An empty list always means
there are no rows. A detail read checks for a failed read before it answers
`NOT_FOUND`.

A collection path with no handler for the verb, such as `GET /user/inventory_item`,
answers HTTP 405. Use the `/list` route.

## Paging and filtering

Every list and report that pages takes `page_num` (1-based, default 1) and
`page_size` (default 50, at most 500). A route with another default or limit
says so. `books_queue` allows up to 1000 and `balance_check` up to 2000. The
reply carries `total_count`, `page_num` and `page_size`. The rows skipped are
`(page_num - 1) * page_size`.

`page` and `limit` are the old names. They are still read for inventory
mobile <= 1.1.0 and are deprecated (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2).

List routes also take `match_filter_dict` (a JSON object), `search_text`,
`sort_dict` (JSON), `get_count`, `ids_list` (a JSON array) and `list_id`.
Report routes that filter read their filters from `match_filter_dict`. The keys
each one reads are listed on the route. A report filter sent as a top-level
query argument still works for one release and is deprecated.

## Dropdowns (picklists)

Every dropdown uses `GET /entity/data?entity_type=<type>&action=picklist`.
It takes `match_filter_dict`, `search_text`, `sort_dict`, `page_num` and
`page_size` (default 1000, at most 1000). The endpoint is documented in the
CRM spec under Entity Data.

The record types below are read through their own service. The caller needs
`R` on the module. Without it the answer is the service's
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_<MODULE>` code with the message "You cannot view this
list." `tenant_scope` is ignored. A failed read answers
`INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`. To look up rows by id, send
`match_filter_dict={"_id": {"$in": ["<hex id>", ...]}}`. Each id may also be
written `"ObjectId('<hex id>')"`.

Record types: `inventory_item`, `inventory_txn`, `inventory_lot`,
`inventory_count_session`, `inventory_count_line`, `inventory_forecast`. Each
row carries `name` and `<entity_type>_id`. `name` joins these parts with ` · `
and skips blank ones:

| entity_type | `name` is built from |
|---|---|
| `inventory_item` | product name (or SKU), site, location, bin |
| `inventory_txn` | product name, `txn_type`, `qty`, `uom` |
| `inventory_lot` | `lot_number`, product name, `expiry_date` |
| `inventory_count_session` | name (or code), `count_date` |
| `inventory_count_line` | product name, `location_code`, session name |
| `inventory_forecast` | product name (or SKU), `site_code`, `period_key` |

The rows are under `data.<entity_type>` (for example `data.inventory_item`),
or under `data.values` when `use_native=false`.

Fixed lists have no records behind them. They answer `action=picklist` only,
and need no `tenant_scope`. The rows are under `data.values`:

| entity_type | `match_filter_dict` keys | Row fields |
|---|---|---|
| `inventory_uom` | `dimension` (`count`, `weight`, `volume`, `length`) | `code`, `label`, `dimension`, `precision`, `is_pack` |
| `inventory_item_type` | none | `code`, `label`, `description`, `example`, `dimensions` |
| `inventory_txn_type` | `hand_entry` (bool) | `code`, `label`, `description`, `action`, `source_type`, `inbound`, `signed_by_caller`, `reason_required`, `moves_to_another_place` |
| `inventory_txn_source_type` | none | `code`, `label`, `books_owns_it` |
| `inventory_txn_reason` | `txn_action`, `txn_type_code` | `code`, `label`, `is_waste` |
| `site` | `include_inactive` (bool) | `code`, `name`, `is_primary`, `is_active` |

```
GET /entity/data?entity_type=inventory_txn_reason&action=picklist&match_filter_dict={"txn_type_code":"waste_issue"}
{"result": 1,
 "data": {"values": [{"code": "spoiled", "label": "Spoiled", "is_waste": true}],
          "total_count": 5},
 "gross_count": 5}
```

`site` returns inactive sites too, unless `include_inactive` is `false`. Its
`data` also carries `codes_enforced`. It is false when the tenant has no
registered sites, and then any site code is accepted.

Any other action on a fixed list answers
`{"result": 2, "ok": false, "error": "invalid_data", "error_code": "INVALID_DATA", "message": "This list supports action=picklist only"}`.

## Deprecated routes

These still work exactly as before for one release. Each call writes a
DEPRECATED line to the server log. They are marked `deprecated` below.

| Deprecated | Use |
|---|---|
| `POST /user/inventory/place/manage` | the place routes under `/user/site/{site_code}/location` |
| `GET /user/inventory_item/picklist` and the other four `<entity>/picklist` routes | `GET /entity/data?entity_type=<entity>&action=picklist` |
| `GET /user/inventory/uom` | `entity_type=inventory_uom` |
| `GET /user/inventory/item_type` | `entity_type=inventory_item_type` |
| `GET /user/inventory/txn_type` | `entity_type=inventory_txn_type` |
| `GET /user/inventory/txn_source_type` | `entity_type=inventory_txn_source_type` |
| `GET /user/inventory/txn_reason` | `entity_type=inventory_txn_reason` |
| `GET /user/inventory/sites` | `entity_type=site` |

An error envelope also carries `status_code` and `request_path`. `status_code`
is 200, except 500 on `INVENTORY_REQUIRES_PRO`. The HTTP status is 200 in both
cases.
An exception the service does not expect answers `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

## Authorization

Two independent mechanisms:

* **`module_access`** decides whether you may do a thing at all —
  `inventory_item: ["A","C","R","U","D"]`.
* **`access_dict` + `site_code`** decides which rows you see.

These routes do not apply `access_dict` or the caller's sites. They read
every row in the company, filtered only by the parameters sent:
`replenishment`, `valuation`, `lcnrv`, `lot_trace`, `lot_reconcile`,
`expiring`, `warranty_expiring`, `scan`, `balance_check`, `books_queue`,
the two matrix GETs (`variants`, `matrix_stock`), and the writes
`consumption_rate`, `expire_lots` and the lot deletes.

Three roles are seeded:

| Role | `inventory_item` | `inventory_txn` | `inventory_count_session` | `product` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inventory_viewer` | `R` | `R` | `R` | `R` |
| `inventory_clerk` | `A C R U` | `A C R` | `A C R U` | `R` |
| `inventory_manager` | `A C R U D` | `A C R` | `A C R U D` | `A C R U D` |

`record_counts` asserts `U` on `inventory_count_session`; `post_session` asserts
`D`. A clerk can scope a stocktake, freeze it and enter every shelf reading, and
cannot post it.

No seeded role has `U` or `D` on `inventory_txn`.

Lot, matrix, stock, forecast estimate, write-down, cost update and place routes
check privileges on `inventory_item`. Lot routes do not read the
`inventory_lot` grant.

Privilege checks **fail closed**: a check that errors denies.

Most writes also check the tenant's plan. A tenant without the Inventory feature
gets `INVENTORY_REQUIRES_PRO` (HTTP 200). Reads, deleting a stock row, cancelling
or deleting a stocktake, place setup and settings do not check the plan.

## Roles and sites

A role carries a site through **`open_assignment_group_code`** (OAG) rather than by
seeding one role per site. `POST /user/inventory_item` and
`POST /user/inventory_count_session` stamp `site_code` by precedence:

1. explicit `site_code` in the payload — always wins
2. the creator's **sole** OAG code, if that code is a registered site in
   `tenant.site_list`
3. empty, meaning unscoped

A movement uses the `site_code` in its payload as sent.

⚠ **An OAG code that is not a registered site is skipped.** The resolver logs a
warning and the record is created with an empty `site_code`.

## Accounting

Movements post to Ambivo Books. Core computes the journal entry and sends it;
Books validates and records it.

| Movement | Entry |
|---|---|
| receipt against a purchase order | Dr Inventory asset / Cr `grni_account_id` |
| receipt with no document, or another source | Dr Inventory asset / Cr `expense_account_id` |
| receipt from a `bill`, `invoice` or `payment` source | not posted (`not_required`) |
| issue | Dr `expense_account_id` / Cr Inventory asset |
| Wasted issue (`waste_issue`) | Dr `waste_account_id` (else `expense_account_id`) / Cr Inventory asset |
| issue to production | Dr WIP / Cr Inventory asset |
| finished goods back | Dr Inventory asset / Cr WIP |
| adjustment or count, shortage | Dr `expense_account_id` / Cr Inventory asset |
| adjustment or count, overage | Dr Inventory asset / Cr `expense_account_id` |
| write-down | Dr `writedown_account_id` (else `expense_account_id`) / Cr Inventory asset |
| transfer between two sites | not sent (see below). The entry it would build is Dr Inventory asset at `to_site` / Cr Inventory asset at `from_site` |

A missing account sets `post_status: failed` with
`post_error: INVENTORY_BOOKS_ACCOUNT_MISSING`. A movement with zero value is marked
`not_required`.

A transfer inside one site is marked `not_required` when it is written. A
transfer between two sites is not sent to Books when it is recorded, and stays
`pending`. `GET /user/inventory/books_queue` shows why in `blocked_reason`. A
blank site at either end shows `NOT_REQUIRED`. Sites in two different Books
companies show `INVENTORY_BOOKS_INTERCOMPANY_ACCOUNT_MISSING`. One site with a
company and one without, on a tenant with several companies, shows
`INVENTORY_BOOKS_TRANSFER_COMPANY_UNRESOLVED`.

**LCNRV is report-only.** `GET /user/inventory/lcnrv` lists stock carried above net
realisable value and writes nothing. `POST /user/inventory/write_down` writes
positions down.

get.description:
Returns balances, not products: one row per (product, site, location, bin).
Default order is `location_code`, `bin_code`, `product_name`. Each row adds
`qty_available`, `unit_cost`, `cost_basis`, `valuation_qty`, `total_value`,
`wip_value` and `below_reorder_point`, computed at read time.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_item`. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

post.summary: Ensure a stock row exists for a product at a place
post.description:
Creates the balance row at zero if it is not there, and returns the existing
row if it is. Needs `C` on `inventory_item`.

The unit, item type, reorder policy and standard cost are copied from the
product. Sending `qty_on_hand` or `opening_qty` is refused with
`INVENTORY_OPENING_QTY_NOT_ALLOWED`. A `non_stock` product is refused with
`INVENTORY_ITEM_NOT_STOCKED`. A missing or malformed `product_id` is refused
with `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_ID_INVALID`. A product that does not exist is refused
with `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`. A product with no unit is refused with
`INVENTORY_UOM_REQUIRED`. A malformed `books_entity_id` is refused with
`INVENTORY_BOOKS_ENTITY_INVALID`. An unregistered `site_code` is refused with
`INVENTORY_SITE_CODE_UNKNOWN` (see the introduction). The place is checked as
stock going in.

Policy fields such as `reorder_point` in the body are ignored. Set them
with `PATCH /user/inventory_item/{item_id}`.

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Created", inventory_item_id, created, inventory_item}`. `created` is false when the row already existed. A row created earlier in the same second also reports `created: true`.

delete.description:
Deletes balance rows, not products. Each id is checked on its own, exactly
as the single delete. A refused id does not stop the others. An unexpected
failure on one id is listed with `DELETE_FAILED`. With no ids the
answer is `INVALID_DATA`.

parameters.name: ids_list
parameters.description: JSON array of stock row ids. `inventory_item_ids` and `inventory_item_ids_list` are accepted too.

200.description: `{result: 1, deleted_ids, refused: [{inventory_item_id, error_code}], deleted_count}`

put.summary: Update reorder policy and descriptive fields (alias of PATCH)
put.description: An exact alias of PATCH, for clients that cannot send one: same body, same behaviour, same refusals.

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Updated", inventory_item_id, inventory_item}`
Envelope keyed `inventory_item`. `NOT_FOUND` when there is no such row.

patch.summary: Update reorder policy and descriptive fields
patch.description:
Needs `U` on `inventory_item`. Only these fields are written, and only
when sent: `reorder_point`, `reorder_quantity`, `safety_stock`,
`lead_time_days`, `max_stock_level`, `preferred_vendor_id`,
`standard_cost`, `is_perishable`, `shelf_life_days`, `valuation_method`,
`notes`, `status`, `tags`, `meta` and `custom_form_dict`.

Any other field is dropped and the answer is still "Updated". Examples
are `qty_on_order`, `last_unit_cost`, `uom`, the place codes,
`currency` and `books_entity_id`. A `tags` that is not a list, or a
`meta` or `custom_form_dict` that is not an object, is dropped too.

`lead_time_days` and `shelf_life_days` are cut to whole days, so 2.9
is saved as 2. A value that is not a number is saved as 0.

A numeric field sent as null or `""` is saved as 0. For
`standard_cost` that can write a `cost_update` movement. Leave a field
out to keep its value.

⚠ **Balance fields are refused.** Sending `qty_on_hand`, `qty_wip`,
`qty_reserved`, `avg_unit_cost`, `cost_basis`, `secondary_qty_on_hand` or
`balance_seq` returns `INVENTORY_BALANCE_NOT_WRITABLE` and saves nothing.
Change a quantity with a movement or a count.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_<FIELD>_INVALID` | `reorder_point`, `reorder_quantity`, `safety_stock`, `max_stock_level` or `standard_cost` is not a number |
| `INVENTORY_<FIELD>_NEGATIVE` | a numeric field is below 0 |
| `INVENTORY_ITEM_STATUS_INVALID` | `status` is not `active`, `inactive` or `discontinued` |
| `INVENTORY_VALUATION_METHOD_UNAVAILABLE` | `valuation_method` is not blank and not `weighted_average` |
| `INVENTORY_ITEM_NOT_FOUND` | no such row in this tenant |

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Updated", inventory_item_id, inventory_item}`

delete.description:
Needs `D` on `inventory_item`. Refused with `INVENTORY_ITEM_HAS_STOCK` while
`qty_on_hand` or `qty_wip` is not zero, or when stock moved there during the
delete. Refused with `INVENTORY_ITEM_HAS_HISTORY` when a movement's plain
`site_code`, `location_code` and `bin_code` match this product at this place.
A row that only sent stock out by transfer has a `balance_seq`. It is refused
with `INVENTORY_ITEM_HAS_STOCK`. Set `status: inactive` to retire a row with
history.

200.description: `{result: 1, inventory_item_id, deleted: true}`

get.description:
Every balance for one product, plus a rollup. Needs `R` on `inventory_item`.
A blank `site_code` includes every site. Passing `location_code` or
`bin_code` narrows to that place; an EMPTY string is a real value (main
area, no bin). Omit the parameter to include every location or bin.

Without `product_id` the answer is `INVALID_DATA`.

200.description: `{result: 1, data: [positions], rollup}`

get.description:
Newest first by default (`timestamp` descending).

Each row carries the running balance fields (see "Running balance on every
movement"): `qty_on_hand_before`, `qty_on_hand_after`, `unit_cost_before`,
`unit_cost_after`, `value_before`, `value_after`, `balance_seq`, or their
`from_*` / `to_*` variants on a transfer. Rows from before the change have
none of them.

A place's history includes transfers OUT of it. A transfer stores its
destination in `site_code` / `location_code` / `bin_code` and its source in
`from_site_code` / `from_location_code` / `from_bin_code`. When
`match_filter_dict` names any of the three plain place fields, and no `from_*`
or `to_*` field, those fields match either end. Read a transfer's figures for
a place from the `from_*` variants when the place is its source, and the
`to_*` variants when it is the destination.

With `ids_list`, the place fields match the destination only. Transfers
out of the place are then left out.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_txn`, with `total_count`, `page_num` and `page_size`. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

post.description:
The only way a balance changes. Needs `C` on `inventory_txn`. There is **no
PATCH and no DELETE** for a movement. A correction is a new offsetting
movement.

Send `txn_type`, or `txn_type_code` from `GET /user/inventory/txn_type`. A
named type sets `txn_type`, and sets `source_entity_type` when none is sent.
The quantity's sign comes from the type: a receipt adds and an issue removes,
whatever sign was sent. `adjustment` and `count` keep the sign sent.

⚠ **Send `client_txn_id` from any client that may retry.** It is the
idempotency key behind a unique index. A repeat of a known `client_txn_id`
returns the original movement with `duplicate: true` and moves nothing.

`adjustment` and `count` need a reason: `reason_code` from
`GET /user/inventory/txn_reason`, or free text in `reason`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_TXN_TYPE_INVALID` | `txn_type` is missing or unknown |
| `INVENTORY_TXN_TYPE_CODE_INVALID` | `txn_type_code` is not registered |
| `INVENTORY_TXN_SOURCE_TYPE_INVALID` | `source_entity_type` is not registered (`GET /user/inventory/txn_source_type`) |
| `INVENTORY_TXN_REASON_CODE_INVALID` | `reason_code` is not registered |
| `INVENTORY_TXN_REASON_REQUIRED` | the type needs a reason and neither `reason` nor `reason_code` was sent |
| `INVENTORY_QTY_REQUIRED`, `INVENTORY_QTY_INVALID`, `INVENTORY_QTY_ZERO` | `qty` is missing, not a number, or rounds to 0 |
| `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_ID_INVALID` | `product_id` is missing or not an id |
| `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` | no such product |
| `INVENTORY_BOOKS_ENTITY_INVALID` | `books_entity_id` is not blank and not all digits |
| `INVENTORY_UOM_REQUIRED` | the product has no unit of measure |
| `INVENTORY_ITEM_NOT_STOCKED` | the product is `non_stock` |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_PARENT_NOT_STOCKED` | the product has options; move a variant |
| `INVENTORY_UOM_UNKNOWN`, `INVENTORY_UOM_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`, `INVENTORY_PACK_SIZE_UNKNOWN` | `uom` cannot be converted to the stocking unit |
| `INVENTORY_WRITEDOWN_WRONG_ENDPOINT` | `txn_type: writedown`; use `POST /user/inventory/write_down` |
| `INVENTORY_COST_UPDATE_WRONG_ENDPOINT` | `txn_type: cost_update`; use `POST /user/inventory/cost_update` |
| `INVENTORY_BALANCE_BUSY` | the position kept changing while this was saved; nothing recorded, safe to retry |
| `INVENTORY_BALANCE_UPDATE_FAILED` | the write failed; nothing recorded. Also when a database error stops the lots being drawn down; the lots already drawn are put back. |
| `INVENTORY_LEDGER_FAULT` | server without transactions only: the balance moved and could not be put back. The row keeps the movement under `ledger_pending` and `GET /user/inventory/balance_check` lists it. The lots drawn for it stay drawn. Do not retry without a `client_txn_id`. |
| `INVENTORY_RECEIPT_USE_GOODS_RECEIPT` | the movement names `source_entity_type: purchase_order`, or the named type `purchase_receipt` with any source. A purchase order is received through goods receipts (`POST /user/goods_receipt`), which also update the order and the amount on order. Nothing recorded. A receipt with no purchase order stays `misc_receipt`. |

The place checks in the introduction apply.

**Lot and serial products.** Stock going out takes the lots named in
`lot_lines`. Without them it takes available, unexpired lots in expiry order,
soonest first. A product with `allocation_strategy: fifo` takes the oldest
receipt first. A product with `allocation_strategy: manual` needs `lot_lines`.
Without `lot_lines`, stock with no lot at that place covers a shortfall.
Lots and stock with no lot are taken only at the exact place of the
movement. A blank location or bin matches only a blank location or bin.
Stock going out of a blank location never takes lots at another location.
Stock coming in goes to the lot in `lot_lines`, `lot_number` or
`scanned_code`. It tops up that lot at this place, or creates it.
An `expiry_date` may be `YYYY-MM-DD` or a JSON number of epoch seconds. A
date typed as digits, such as `20300131`, is refused.

These refusals come before anything moves:

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_SERIAL_REQUIRES_DISCRETE` | the product is serial-tracked but measured, or its unit allows decimals |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_INSUFFICIENT` | lots and stock with no lot cannot cover the quantity |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_LINES_REQUIRED` | the product is picked by hand and `lot_lines` is empty |
| `INVENTORY_SERIAL_QTY_FRACTIONAL` | a serial product goes out in a part of a unit |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_LINE_INVALID` | a `lot_lines` entry is not an object |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_NUMBER_REQUIRED` | a `lot_lines` entry has no `lot_number`. On a receipt, an entry with a `serial_number` passes. |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_LINE_DUPLICATE` | one lot number is on two lines |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_NOT_FOUND` | a named lot is not at this place |
| `INVENTORY_SERIAL_ELSEWHERE` | a named serial is at another place (site, location and bin compared exactly) |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_NOT_PICKABLE` | a named lot is not `available` |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_EXPIRED` | a named lot is past its expiry date |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_LINE_QTY_INVALID` | a line quantity is 0 or not a number |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_LINE_OVERDRAWN` | a line takes more than the lot has free |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_LINES_MISMATCH` | the line quantities do not add up to `qty` |
| `INVENTORY_SERIAL_REQUIRED` | a serial receipt names no serial number |
| `INVENTORY_SERIAL_ONE_PER_LINE` | a serial receipt without `lot_lines` has a `qty` other than 1 |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_REQUIRED` | the product has `lot_required_on_receipt` and the receipt names no lot |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_NOT_RECEIVABLE` | the receiving lot is `expired`, `recalled`, `damaged` or `quarantine` |
| `INVENTORY_SERIAL_ALREADY_ON_HAND` | the serial being received is already on hand. On a transfer, a second on-hand row for the same serial. |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_DATE_INVALID` | stock coming in has an `expiry_date` or `expiry_ts` that cannot be read |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_CONCURRENT_CHANGE` | another movement took from a picked lot after it was picked. The lots already drawn are put back. |

A receipt that names no lot, for a product without `lot_required_on_receipt`,
moves the stock with no lot and adds `lot_warning`.

A transfer of a serial number moves the unit's lot row to the destination.
A transfer of a lot draws the lot down at the source and adds the same
quantity to that lot at the destination.

**Wasted.** Send `txn_type_code: waste_issue` for stock that spoiled, broke,
expired or was thrown away. It is an `issue` in every way (places, lots,
running balance, idempotency) and needs a reason: `reason_code` from
`GET /user/inventory/txn_reason?txn_type_code=waste_issue`, or free text in
`reason`. Without one: `INVENTORY_TXN_REASON_REQUIRED`. The row keeps
`txn_type_code: waste_issue`, so reports and charts can group waste apart
from `misc_issue` (Issue). Books debits the item's
`waste_account_id` when it names one, otherwise `expense_account_id`,
exactly like any issue.

⚠ **`unit_cost` is a rate in the UoM you are sending.** If `uom` differs from
the product's stocking unit, the quantity **and** the cost are converted by
the same factor, so the extended value stays the same.

200.description:
`{result: 1, message: "Recorded", inventory_txn_id, inventory_txn, qty_on_hand, unit_cost, cost_basis}`.
A transfer returns `from_qty_on_hand` and `to_qty_on_hand` in place of
`qty_on_hand` and `cost_basis`. A tracked product adds `tracking_mode` and
`lot_list`. A replay returns `{inventory_txn_id, duplicate: true, inventory_txn}`.

qty_on_hand.description: The position's balance after the movement.

from_qty_on_hand.description: Transfer only. The source balance after.

to_qty_on_hand.description: Transfer only. The destination balance after.

lot_warning.description: Present when a tracked product moved without a lot number. Never on a transfer.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_txn`. `NOT_FOUND` when there is no such row.

get.description:
Newest `count_date` first by default.

Each row names who worked on the session. `created_by_userid` is who
scoped it. `updated_by_userid` is who last changed it: editing the session
and recording counts both stamp it.

`counted_by_userid_list` holds everyone who has entered a count on a line
in this session. The list only grows. A recount replaces the counter on the
line, and the earlier counter stays on the session.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_count_session`, with `total_count`, `page_num` and `page_size`. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

post.description:
Creates the session in **draft**. Needs `C` on `inventory_count_session`.
Nothing is frozen and no lines exist yet; that happens at `/open`.

`period_type` is `week` (default), `biweek`, `month`, `quarter`, `year` or
`adhoc`. `count_date` defaults to today in the tenant's time zone. A blank
`name` becomes a default such as `Week count <period_key>`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_COUNT_TYPE_INVALID` | `count_type` is not `full`, `cycle` or `spot` |
| `INVENTORY_PERIOD_TYPE_INVALID` | `period_type` is not in the list above |
| `INVENTORY_COUNT_DATE_INVALID` | `count_date` cannot be read, or `week_start_day` is not an integer |
| `INVENTORY_COUNT_CODE_DUPLICATE` | another session in the tenant has this `code` |
| `BOOKS_ENTITY_ID_MUST_BE_THE_NUMERIC_ID_OF_AN_AMBIVO_BOOKS_COMPANY_OR_OMITTED_TO_USE_THIS_TENANTS_DEFAULT` | `books_entity_id` is not blank and not all digits. This route has no shorter code for it. |
| `INVENTORY_SITE_CODE_UNKNOWN`, `INVENTORY_LOCATION_UNKNOWN`, `INVENTORY_BIN_UNKNOWN` | a scope code is not registered. Locations and bins are checked only at a registered site. With no location scoped, a bin passes if any location at the site has it. |

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Created", inventory_count_session_id, inventory_count_session}`

delete.description:
Each id goes through the single delete on its own: `D` on
`inventory_count_session`, lines deleted first, refused once posted. A
refused id does not stop the others. A posted stocktake is listed with
`INVENTORY_COUNT_ALREADY_POSTED`, an unknown id with
`INVENTORY_COUNT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, and an unexpected failure with
`DELETE_FAILED`. With no ids the answer is `INVALID_DATA`.

parameters.name: ids_list
parameters.description: JSON array of stocktake ids. `inventory_count_session_ids` and `inventory_count_session_ids_list` are accepted too.

200.description: `{result: 1, deleted_ids, refused: [{inventory_count_session_id, error_code}], deleted_count}`

get.description: The same fields as the list route, `created_by_userid`, `updated_by_userid` and `counted_by_userid_list` among them.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_count_session`. `NOT_FOUND` when there is no such row.

patch.summary: Edit a stocktake, or cancel it via `status`
patch.description:
Needs `U` on `inventory_count_session`.

`{"status": "cancelled", "cancel_reason": "..."}` cancels the session. Its lines
are kept and nothing is posted. The answer is
`{result: 1, message: "Cancelled", inventory_count_session_id, cancelled: true}`.
Any other field in a cancel body is ignored. Any `status` other than
`cancelled` is ignored, and the answer is still "Updated".

Otherwise `name`, `description`, `notes`, `code` and `count_type` can change
while the session is not posted or cancelled. A blank `name` gets the default
name. The scope fields (`location_code`, `location_code_list`,
`bin_code_list`, `category_sku_list`, `product_ids_list`,
`include_zero_qty`, `period_type`, `count_date`) change only in `draft`.
After that, sending `location_code_list`, `category_sku_list`,
`product_ids_list`, `include_zero_qty`, `period_type` or `count_date` is
refused with `INVENTORY_COUNT_SCOPE_LOCKED`. `location_code` and
`bin_code_list` are ignored.

`count_type: ""` is saved as a blank type. `include_zero_qty` is off
only for a JSON `false`.

`week_start_day` is not stored. It is read only when the same body
changes `period_type` or `count_date`. A change to either without it
recomputes the period with week start 0. Send `week_start_day` again
with every period change.

Refusals: `INVENTORY_COUNT_ALREADY_POSTED`, `INVENTORY_COUNT_CANCELLED`,
`INVENTORY_COUNT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `INVENTORY_COUNT_CODE_DUPLICATE`,
`INVENTORY_COUNT_TYPE_INVALID`, `INVENTORY_PERIOD_TYPE_INVALID`,
`INVENTORY_COUNT_DATE_INVALID` and the scope place codes. A cancel is refused
only with `INVENTORY_COUNT_ALREADY_POSTED` or
`INVENTORY_COUNT_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`.

week_start_day.description: Not stored. Read only with `period_type` or `count_date` in the same body.

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Updated", inventory_count_session_id, inventory_count_session}`

delete.summary: Delete a stocktake and its lines
delete.description:
Needs `D` on `inventory_count_session`. Refused once posted with
`INVENTORY_COUNT_ALREADY_POSTED`. The lines are deleted first. If that fails
the answer is `INVENTORY_COUNT_LINE_DELETE_FAILED` and the session stays.

200.description: `{result: 1, inventory_count_session_id, deleted: true}`

post.summary: Freeze the session and materialise its count lines
post.description:
Needs `U` on `inventory_count_session`. Writes one line per stock row in
scope, with the expected quantity and unit cost as they stand **at this
moment**, then sets the session to `open`.

The scope is the site, the locations, bins, categories and products named on
the session. A session with a blank site takes stock rows from every site. Inactive and `non_stock` rows are left out. Rows at zero are left
out when `include_zero_qty` is false. Rows with status `discontinued`
get count lines.

A later posting compares the counted quantity with this snapshot.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_COUNT_ALREADY_OPEN` | the session is not in `draft`. A cancelled session gets this code too. |
| `INVENTORY_COUNT_SCOPE_EMPTY` | no stock rows are in scope |
| `INVENTORY_COUNT_TOO_MANY_LINES` | more than 5000 stock rows are in scope |

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Opened", inventory_count_session_id, line_count, previous_session_id, period_days, inventory_count_session}`

post.description:
Needs `U` on `inventory_count_session`. The session must be `draft`, `open`,
`counting` or `counted`, or the answer is `INVENTORY_COUNT_NOT_EDITABLE`.
A draft has no lines, so each entry is refused with
`INVENTORY_COUNT_LINE_NOT_FOUND`.
Recording a count does **not** move a balance. Nothing changes until `/post`.

Each entry names its line by `inventory_count_line_id`, or by `product_id`
with `location_code` and `bin_code`. A blank location or bin matches blank. `counted_qty` is in
`uom`, which defaults to the line's unit. `{"skip": true, "skip_reason": "..."}`
marks a line skipped. Send `skip` as a JSON boolean. Any truthy value,
such as the string `"false"`, skips the line.

A line whose count differs from a positive expected quantity by more than 25% gets
status `recount` and `recount_requested: true`. A catch-weight line needs
`secondary_qty`.

Each entry is applied or refused on its own. A body with no entries answers
`INVALID_DATA`. The old body key `data` still works in place of `counts`.
It is deprecated (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2).

Per-entry refusals: `INVENTORY_COUNT_LINE_REF_REQUIRED` (no line id and no
`product_id`), `INVENTORY_COUNT_LINE_ID_INVALID`,
`INVENTORY_COUNT_LINE_NOT_FOUND`, `INVENTORY_COUNT_QTY_REQUIRED`,
`INVENTORY_COUNT_QTY_INVALID`, `INVENTORY_COUNT_QTY_NEGATIVE`,
`INVENTORY_CATCH_WEIGHT_REQUIRED`, `INVENTORY_COUNT_ENTRY_INVALID` (not an
object), `INVENTORY_COUNT_ENTRY_FAILED`, and
`INVENTORY_UOM_UNKNOWN` or another unit code when `uom` cannot be converted.

counted_ts.description: Epoch seconds. Defaults to now. Send seconds: milliseconds give a far-future date, and an ISO date string is read as now.

skip.description: Send a JSON boolean. The string `"false"` counts as true.

200.description:
`{result: 1, applied_count, refused_count, data, inventory_count_session}`.
Each `data` entry is `{result: 1, inventory_count_line_id, counted_qty, variance_qty, variance_value, recount_requested}`,
`{result: 1, inventory_count_line_id, skipped: true}`, or
`{result: 2, error_code, entry}`.

post.summary: Apply the count: write balances and count movements
post.description:
Needs `D` on `inventory_count_session`. The only step that changes a
balance. Each counted line with a variance becomes a `count` movement for the
variance quantity, dated at the line's `counted_ts`. A line with no variance
is marked posted and writes no movement.

The variance value on each line uses the line's own snapshotted unit cost for
both the expected and the counted quantity.

Uncounted lines are never posted. While any line is neither counted nor
skipped, the answer is `INVENTORY_COUNT_INCOMPLETE`, unless the body sends
`{"force": true}`. With `force`, only counted lines post. Send `force`
as a JSON boolean. Any truthy value counts, so the string `"false"`
posts an incomplete count.

A line that fails to post is listed in `refused`, and the session is still
marked `posted`. `total_variance_value`, `total_shrink_value` and the
session's `variance_line_count` include refused lines. The session's
`books_accounting_status` is set from those totals, so it can be
`pending` for stock that never moved.

After posting, the period close and next forecast run; a
failure there is reported in `forecast` and does not undo the posting.

Refusals: `INVENTORY_COUNT_ALREADY_POSTED`, `INVENTORY_COUNT_CANCELLED`,
`INVENTORY_COUNT_NOT_OPEN` (still `draft`), `INVENTORY_COUNT_NOTHING_COUNTED`.

force.description: Send a JSON boolean. The string `"false"` counts as true.

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Posted", inventory_count_session_id, posted_line_count, refused, uncounted_line_count, total_variance_value, total_shrink_value, forecast, inventory_count_session}`

get.description:
Ordered by `location_code`, `bin_code`, `product_name` by default. The
default page size is 200.

Each line names the people on it. `counted_by_userid` is who entered the
count that stands. `created_by_userid` is who froze the line when the
session opened. `updated_by_userid` is who last changed it: freezing the
line, posting it and renaming the session all stamp it.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: JSON filter. Usually {"inventory_count_session_id":"..."}

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page. Above 500 is treated as 500.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_count_line`, with `total_count`, `page_num` and `page_size`. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

get.description:
The same fields as the list route. GET only: readings are recorded with
`POST /user/inventory_count_session/{session_id}/counts`, and lines are
deleted with their stocktake.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_count_line`. `NOT_FOUND` when there is no such row. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

get.description:
Newest `period_end_date` first by default. On a closed period `bias` is
`on_track`, `under`, `over` or `no_forecast`. An open period has a blank `bias`. A period with no forecast has `no_forecast` and a
null `variance_pct`.

**The manager's estimate travels with the row.** An open row carries the
estimate the blend used, copied from the stock row: `manual_rate_per_day`,
`manual_rate_entered_qty` ("10" of "10 lb a week"),
`manual_rate_period_type` (`week`), `manual_rate_userid` (who typed it) and
`manual_rate_ts`. Closing the period keeps the same five on the closed row.

`created_by_userid` is who first wrote the row. A later close into the same
open period keeps it. `updated_by_userid` is who last wrote the row.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_forecast`, with `total_count`, `page_num` and `page_size`. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

get.description:
The same fields as the list route. GET only: forecasts are computed when
a stocktake posts. To change what is expected, set the consumption
estimate with `PUT /user/inventory/consumption_rate`.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_forecast`. `NOT_FOUND` when there is no such row. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

put.summary: Set the manager's own consumption estimate
put.description:
Needs `U` on `inventory_item`. "About ten pounds a week" is
`{"qty": 10, "period_type": "week"}`. The estimate is stored as a daily rate
on every stock row for the product at that site and location, under
`meta.manual_rate_per_day`. A blank `site_code` means stock held at no site.
It writes only those rows.

The same rows keep what was typed and who typed it:
`meta.manual_rate_entered_qty`, `meta.manual_rate_period_type`,
`meta.manual_rate_userid` and `meta.manual_rate_ts`. The row's
`updated_by_userid` becomes the caller. Forecasts copy the five `meta`
values onto the period row they open.

Forecasts blend the estimate with the observed rate. The estimate's weight is
100% at confidence `none`, 70% at `low`, 30% at `medium` and 0 at `high`.
With no observed rate the estimate is used alone. With no estimate the
observed rate is used alone. An estimate of 0 counts as no estimate,
so `qty: 0` leaves the observed rate alone.

The rows are matched in the whole company. Site access is not checked.

The checks run in this order: `period_type`, then `qty`, then
`product_id`. An empty body answers `INVENTORY_QTY_INVALID`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_ID_REQUIRED` | `product_id` is missing |
| `INVENTORY_PERIOD_TYPE_INVALID` | `period_type` is not `week`, `biweek`, `month`, `quarter` or `year` |
| `INVENTORY_QTY_INVALID`, `INVENTORY_QTY_NEGATIVE` | `qty` is missing, not a number, or below 0 |
| `INVENTORY_ITEM_NOT_FOUND` | no stock row for the product at that site and location. With a blank `site_code`, no row held at no site. |

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Saved", product_id, site_code, location_code, rate_per_day, entered_qty, period_type, matched_count}`

get.summary: What to buy, and by when
get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. Reads up to 1000 stock rows that are not
`inactive`, in id order, then returns those that need reordering now.
`scan_truncated` is true when the read returns 1000 rows. The plan may
then be partial. With `horizon_days`, it also returns
rows whose days of cover is within `horizon_days` plus the lead time.
A `horizon_days` that is not a number counts as 0.

Reads every stock row in the company, filtered only by `site_code` and
`location_code`. Site access is not checked.

Sorted by `replenish_by_date` (projected stockout minus lead time). A row with
no date sorts last.

`days_of_cover` is null and `days_of_cover_known` is false when there is no
consumption rate.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Plan rows per page. Above 500 is treated as 500.

200.description:
`{result: 1, data, total_count, page_num, page_size, count, estimated_total, scan_truncated}`.
`data` is one page of the plan. `total_count` and `estimated_total`
cover every page of the plan as scanned. `scan_truncated` is true when
the scan read 1000 rows, even if that was every row. `count` is the rows on this page,
kept for old clients.
A failed read answers `INVENTORY_REPLENISHMENT_QUERY_FAILED`. Each row carries
`inventory_item_id`, `product_id`, `product_name`, `sku`, `site_code`,
`location_code`, `item_type`, `uom`, `uom_precision`, `qty_on_hand`,
`qty_on_order`, `rate_per_day`, `forecast_source`, `forecast_confidence`,
`days_of_cover`, `days_of_cover_known`, `projected_stockout_date`,
`replenish_by_date`, `suggested_order_qty`, `unit_cost`, `cost_basis`,
`estimated_cost`, `currency`, `reorder_due`, `reasons` and
`preferred_vendor_id`.

get.summary: Stock value, split by cost basis and by site
get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. A **live** figure over rows that are not
`inactive`, not an as-of-date valuation.

`estimated_basis_value` is the value resting on `standard` or `none` cost.
Rows with a negative balance are listed in `negative_positions` (first 50)
and counted in `negative_position_count`.

Reads every stock row in the company, filtered only by `site_code` and
`location_code`. Site access is not checked.

200.description: `{result: 1, total_value, wip_value, on_hand_plus_wip, by_cost_basis, by_site, position_count, estimated_basis_value, estimated_basis_pct, negative_positions, negative_position_count, is_live_valuation}`. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_VALUATION_QUERY_FAILED`.

get.summary: Stock carried above net realisable value (report only)
get.description:
**Lower of Cost or Net Realisable Value** (ASC 330-10-35-1B). Needs `R` on
`inventory_item`. Compares the unit cost of each row that is not `inactive` with the product's
selling price less `cost_to_sell_pct`.

⚠ **This does not write anything down.** `posts_anything` is always false.
Write down with `POST /user/inventory/write_down`.

Each row has `status` `impaired`, `ok` or `no_selling_price`. A product with
**no selling price** has `selling_price`, `nrv_unit` and `nrv_value` null.
Rows with `ok` are left out unless `include_ok` is true. Rows are sorted by
`writedown_value`, largest first.

Reads every stock row in the company, filtered only by `site_code` and
`location_code`. Site access is not checked.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: With neither `page_num` nor `page_size`, the whole list comes back as one page.

200.description:
`{result: 1, data, total_count, page_num, page_size, counts, carrying_value_by_status, total_writedown_indicated, unpriced_positions, posts_anything: false, write_down_endpoint, note}`.
With no paging argument, `data` is the whole list. With one, only
`data` is paged. The totals cover every position. Refusals:
`INVENTORY_LCNRV_QUERY_FAILED`, `INVENTORY_LCNRV_PRODUCT_LOOKUP_FAILED`.

get.description:
Ordered by `expiry_ts` ascending by default. Rows add `qty_available`,
`lot_value`, `days_to_expiry`, `is_expired`, `warranty_days_remaining` and
`in_warranty`.

**One entity carries both.** A serial number is a lot of exactly one, and
`tracking_mode` separates them:

| | `lot` | `serial` |
|---|---|---|
| `qty_on_hand` | any quantity at the product's precision | only ever 0 or 1 |
| `lot_number` unique per | (product, site, location, bin) | product |

A lot row belongs to one place. Supplier lot `A7` delivered to two warehouses
is two rows. A transfer of a serial number moves its one row to the
destination (see `POST /user/inventory_txn`).

Every row carries `created_by_userid` and `updated_by_userid`. Drawing
stock from a lot, putting it back, restating its value, setting a warranty
start and the expiry sweep all stamp `updated_by_userid` with the caller.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_lot`, with `total_count`, `page_num` and `page_size`. A failed read answers `INVENTORY_READ_FAILED`.

post.summary: Refused — a lot is created by receiving stock
post.description:
There is no create route. A lot is created by a receipt that carries a lot
number.

Answers `INVENTORY_LOT_NO_DIRECT_CREATE` and names the route to use instead:
post a receipt to `/user/inventory_txn` carrying a lot number.

200.description: Envelope carrying INVENTORY_LOT_NO_DIRECT_CREATE

delete.summary: Batch delete lots that never held stock
delete.description:
Needs `D` on `inventory_item`. A lot is refused while `qty_on_hand` is not
zero, and also when `qty_received` is not zero. Refused lots are listed in
`refused` and the answer is still `result: 1`. With no ids the answer is
`INVALID_DATA`. Any lot in the company can be deleted. Site access is
not checked.

parameters.name: ids_list
parameters.description: JSON array of lot ids. `inventory_lot_ids` and `inventory_lot_ids_list` are accepted too.

200.description: `{result: 1, deleted, deleted_count, refused: [{id, lot_number, reason}], refused_count}`. A lot that is not found has no `lot_number`, and `reason` is `Not found`.

get.description: The same fields as the list route, `created_by_userid` and `updated_by_userid` among them.

200.description: Envelope keyed `inventory_lot`. `NOT_FOUND` when there is no such row.

patch.summary: Update a lot's status and paperwork
patch.description:
Needs `U` on `inventory_item`.

⚠ **Balance fields are refused.** Sending `qty_on_hand`, `qty_reserved`,
`qty_received`, `unit_cost`, `stock_value`, `base_stock_value`,
`base_unit_cost`, `product_id`, `lot_number` or `tracking_mode` returns
`INVENTORY_LOT_BALANCE_READ_ONLY`.

`status` is `available`, `quarantine`, `expired`, `recalled`, `consumed` or
`damaged`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_LOT_STATUS_INVALID` | `status` is not in the list |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_RECALL_IRREVERSIBLE` | a `recalled` lot is set straight to `available`. Only that one step is refused. `recalled` to `quarantine` and then `available` is allowed, and so is `expired` to `available`. |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_NOT_EMPTY` | `consumed` is set while the lot holds stock |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_DATE_INVALID` | a date cannot be read |
| `INVENTORY_LOT_NOT_FOUND` | no such lot |

The field changes are saved before the status change is checked.

Send dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `YYYY/MM/DD`, `MM/DD/YYYY` and `DD-MM-YYYY`
are also read, so `01-02-2027` is 1 February.

The reason for a status change goes in `status_reason`. A `reason`
field is ignored. `warranty_type` is not checked against its list.
`meta` and `custom_form_dict` replace the whole stored value.

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Updated", inventory_lot}`

delete.summary: Delete one lot that never held stock
delete.description: Same rules and answer shape as the batch delete.

200.description: `{result: 1, deleted, deleted_count, refused, refused_count}`

get.summary: Find every lot row with a lot number
get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. Matches `lot_number` **and**
`supplier_lot_number`. Returns at most 500 rows. `lot_count`,
`qty_on_hand` and `place_list` are worked out from those rows only, and
no flag says when more exist. Without `lot_number` the
answer is `INVENTORY_LOT_NUMBER_REQUIRED` with the message "Enter a lot number."

Reads every lot in the company, filtered only by `lot_number` and
`product_id`. Site access is not checked.

200.description: `{result: 1, lot_number, lot_list, lot_count, qty_on_hand, place_list: [{site_code, location_code}]}`

get.summary: Compare lot balances with the stock rows
get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. Sums `qty_on_hand` over the product's stock
rows and over its lots, in every lot status, for the place given. Blank place
codes include every value. `untracked_qty` is the stock total minus the lot
total.

Reads every row in the company, filtered only by the parameters sent.
Site access is not checked.

parameters.name: product_id
parameters.description: Blank is refused with `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_REQUIRED` and the message "Choose a product."

200.description: `{result: 1, product_id, site_code, location_code, stock_qty, lot_qty, lot_count, untracked_qty, in_balance}`

get.summary: Lots expiring inside a window, soonest first
get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. Lots with stock, in status `available`,
`quarantine` or `expired`, whose `expiry_ts` is on or before now plus `days`.
⚠ **Already-expired lots are included.**

Reads every lot in the company, filtered only by `days` and `site_code`.
Site access is not checked.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Send a whole number. A decimal such as `7.5` counts as 30, and a blank `days=` counts as 0.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: JSON. One key: `site_code`. Other keys are ignored.

parameters.name: site_code
parameters.description: Deprecated. Send it in `match_filter_dict`.

200.description: `{result: 1, lot_list, total_count, page_num, page_size, count, as_of_ts, days}`. `count` equals `total_count` and is kept for old clients.

get.summary: Lots whose warranty ends inside a window
get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. Lots and serials with a `warranty_end_ts` on or
before now plus `days`, soonest first. Warranties that already ended are
included.

Reads every lot in the company, filtered only by `days` and `site_code`.
Site access is not checked.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Send a whole number. A decimal such as `7.5` counts as 30, and a blank `days=` counts as 0.

parameters.name: match_filter_dict
parameters.description: JSON. One key: `site_code`. Other keys are ignored.

200.description: `{result: 1, lot_list, total_count, page_num, page_size, count, as_of_ts, days}`. `count` equals `total_count` and is kept for old clients.

post.description:
Needs `U` on `inventory_item`. Sets `status: expired` on every lot in status
`available` or `quarantine` that holds stock and whose expiry date has
passed. **Idempotent and safe to re-run.** It acts on every lot in the
company. Site access is not checked.

Picking already skips lots past their expiry date, whatever their status.

200.description: `{result: 1, expired}`: how many lots changed.

get.summary: Resolve a scanned code to a product, and to a lot when the label had one
get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. Reads only.

The service parses the code. A GS1 label yields its GTIN, lot or serial
number and expiry. A valid GTIN is looked up by `gtin` and `barcode_list`, in
its 14, 13, 12 and 8 digit forms. If that finds nothing, the code is looked
up by `gtin`, `barcode_list` and `sku`. The lot is found by the parsed lot or
serial number, or else by the code as `lot_number` or `supplier_lot_number`.
`site_code` narrows the lot search. When only a lot is found, the product is
the lot's product. For a valid GTIN, these later lookups use its 14-digit
form in place of the raw scan.

Send the code exactly as the scanner produced it, including any separators.
A blank code returns `product` and `lot` as null.

Searches every product and lot in the company. Site access is not
checked.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The scanned code. Blank returns `product` and `lot` as null.

200.description: `{result: 1, scan, product, lot}`, plus `product_id` and `tracking_mode` when a product is found, and `lot_id` when a lot is found.

get.summary: A parent's child products, in the grid's own option order
get.description: No privilege check beyond sign-in. Variants with status `inactive` are left out unless `include_inactive` is true. `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` when there is no such product. Reads every product in the company. Site access is not checked.

200.description: `{result: 1, parent_id, parent_name, matrix_option_dict, variant_list, count}`

post.summary: Generate the child products for an option grid
post.description:
Needs `C` on `inventory_item`.

Additive: cells that already exist are left alone, and cells removed from the
grid are **not** deleted.

Without `matrix_option_dict` the parent's stored grid is used. Send `dry_run`
to see what would be created before creating it. Send `dry_run` as a
JSON boolean. Any truthy value, such as the string `"false"`, runs a
dry run.

A run that is not a dry run sets `is_matrix_parent: true` on the parent and
stores the grid on it. From then on, movements and cost updates for the
parent are refused with `INVENTORY_MATRIX_PARENT_NOT_STOCKED`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` | no such product |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_OPTIONS_REQUIRED` | no options |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_OPTION_EMPTY` | an option has no values |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_TOO_MANY` | more than 500 cells |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_OPTIONS_COLLIDE` | two new cells get the same name or SKU |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_SKU_TAKEN` | a new SKU is used by another product |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_NAME_TAKEN` | a new name is used by another product |

matrix_option_dict.description: Option name to its values, e.g. `{"Size": ["S","M"], "Colour": ["Red"]}`.

dry_run.description: Send a JSON boolean. The string `"false"` counts as true.

200.description:
`{result: 1, message: "Generated", parent_id, created, already_exist, total_cells, variant_list}`.
A dry run returns `would_create` in place of `created`. Its
`message` is also "Generated", though nothing was created.

get.summary: On-hand quantity for every variant, ready to render as a grid
get.description: No privilege check beyond sign-in. Variants with status `inactive` are left out. Reads every stock row in the company, filtered only by `site_code`. Site access is not checked.

200.description: `{result: 1, parent_id, parent_name, matrix_option_dict, variant_list, count, axis_list, site_code}`. Each variant adds `qty_on_hand`.

get.description:
Active locations only unless `include_inactive` is `true`, `1` or `yes`. At most 500 rows; `total_count` is the full count.

To pick the site, use `GET /entity/data?entity_type=site&action=picklist`.
It includes inactive sites unless `include_inactive` is `false`.
`GET /user/site/picklist` (CRM spec) does the opposite: it hides
inactive sites unless `include_inactive=true`.

200.description:
`{result: 1, location: [...], site_code, total_count}`. Refusals:
`SITE_CODE_REQUIRED`, `SITE_CODE_NOT_FOUND`.

get.description:

Tenant admin, or `U` on `inventory_item`. Only the fields sent change.
A body with none of `name`, `kind` or `bins_required` changes nothing
and still answers `result: 1`. `is_active` cannot be set here. Sending it answers `INVALID_DATA` with the
message "Active status cannot be changed here. Delete the place instead."

Refused with `INVENTORY_PLACE_HAS_STOCK` while any balance there, bins
included, has a nonzero `qty_on_hand`, `qty_wip`, `qty_reserved` or
`qty_on_order`. `data` adds `qty_on_hand` and `position_count`. Other

post.summary: Add, rename, set bins required on, or delete a location or bin
post.description:
Deprecated. Kept for inventory mobile <= 1.1.0 (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2). Use the place routes under `/user/site/{site_code}/location`.

Each write names one site and changes only that site. Two people editing
places at once do not overwrite each other.

Privilege: tenant admin, or `U` on module `inventory_item`. Anyone else gets
the normal `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_INVENTORY_ITEM` refusal.

| action | uses |
|---|---|
| `add_location` | `location_code`, `name`, `kind`, `bins_required` |
| `update_location` | `name`, `kind`, `bins_required` |
| `delete_location` | removes the location and its bins |
| `add_bin` | `bin_code`, `name` |
| `update_bin` | `bin_code`, `name` |
| `delete_bin` | `bin_code` |

Refusals (each carries `site_code`, `location_code`, `bin_code` in `data`):
`SITE_CODE_NOT_FOUND`, `LOCATION_CODE_REQUIRED`, `LOCATION_CODE_EXISTS`,
`LOCATION_CODE_NOT_FOUND`, `BIN_CODE_REQUIRED`, `BIN_CODE_EXISTS`,
`BIN_CODE_NOT_FOUND`, `INVENTORY_PLACE_HAS_STOCK` (a delete while any balance
there, bins included, has nonzero `qty_on_hand`, `qty_wip`, `qty_reserved` or
`qty_on_order`; `data` adds `qty_on_hand` and `position_count`), and
`INVENTORY_BINS_REQUIRED_HAS_UNBINNED_STOCK` (turning on `bins_required` while
stock sits there with no bin; same extra `data`).
`INVENTORY_PLACE_ACTION_INVALID` (an unknown `action`) carries no `data`.
`INTERNAL_ERROR` on an unexpected failure.

get.summary: Positions whose balance_seq has no movement behind it
get.description:
Read only. For each position with a `balance_seq`, the movements carrying that
position's figures must number exactly 1..balance_seq. Reports
`missing_seq`, `duplicate_seq`, `extra_seq`, and `pending` (a movement still
parked on the balance row by a server without transactions). Needs `R` on
`inventory_item`. `missing_seq`, `duplicate_seq` and `extra_seq` each
list at most 50 numbers per position.

`site_code`. Site access is not checked.

`{result: 1, checked_count, problem_count, truncated, data: [...], total_count, page_num, page_size}`.

`product_id`, `name`, `sku`, `category_sku`, `uom`, `uom_precision`,

post.summary: Write impaired positions down to net realisable value
post.description:
Needs `D` on `inventory_item`. Reduces carrying value, writes a `writedown`
movement per position, and offers each one to Books.

⭐⭐ **The caller names the positions, never the amount.** The server re-runs
the impairment test on each position and computes the write-down itself.

The request is refused whole with `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_INVENTORY_ITEM`
(no `D` on `inventory_item`), `INVENTORY_REQUIRES_PRO` (the plan has no
Inventory), `INVENTORY_WRITEDOWN_IDS_REQUIRED` (no ids),
`INVENTORY_WRITEDOWN_BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (more than 200) or
`INVENTORY_WRITEDOWN_REASON_REQUIRED` (blank `reason`).

Otherwise each position is written down or refused on its own, and the answer
is `result: 1`. Per-position refusals: `INVENTORY_LCNRV_NOT_IMPAIRED` (already
at or below NRV), `INVENTORY_LCNRV_NO_SELLING_PRICE`,
`INVENTORY_LCNRV_NOTHING_ON_HAND`, `INVENTORY_LCNRV_BELOW_ROUNDING`,
`INVENTORY_ITEM_NOT_FOUND`, `INVENTORY_ITEM_ID_INVALID`,
`INVENTORY_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND`, `INVENTORY_BALANCE_BUSY`,
`INVENTORY_BALANCE_UPDATE_FAILED`, `INVENTORY_LEDGER_FAULT`,
`INVENTORY_WRITEDOWN_FAILED` and the place error codes.

Each written-down position's movement carries `qty_on_hand_before` equal to
`qty_on_hand_after`, and the unit cost and value before and after. The row's
`cost_basis` becomes `net_realizable_value`.

200.description:
`{result: 1, message: "Written down", written_count, refused_count, total_writedown_value, currency, data}`.
A written entry is `{result: 1, inventory_item_id, inventory_txn_id, product_id, product_name, sku, prior_unit_cost, nrv_unit, valuation_qty, writedown_value, currency, cost_basis_before}`.
A refused entry is `{result: 2, inventory_item_id, error_code, message, data?}`.

post.summary: Set a new unit cost on an item's stock (Cost update)
post.description:
The value changes; the quantity does not. Writes ONE `cost_update` movement
(`txn_type` and `txn_type_code` both `cost_update`, `source_entity_type`
`inventory`) per place (site + location + bin) whose unit cost actually
changes, places with nothing on hand included. Each has `qty: 0`,
`qty_on_hand_before == qty_on_hand_after`, `unit_cost_before`,
`unit_cost_after` (the new cost), `value_before`, `value_after` and the
place's next `balance_seq`. `total_value` is the size of the value change;
its direction is `value_after - value_before`.

All places and all movements go through one ledger write. On a server
with transactions they commit together or not at all. On a server without
them, a write that cannot be put back answers `INVENTORY_LEDGER_FAULT`. A
receipt or issue landing on the same place at the same moment makes the
write start again from a fresh read.

The place's cost afterwards is exactly `unit_cost`: its average cost is set
to it, so the next receipt blends with it. A cost of 0 on a place that is not
written down also clears its last receipt cost and estimated cost. No place
is costed per lot: a lot keeps the cost it was received at.

**Idempotent on `client_txn_id`.** The first movement carries it and the
rest carry `<client_txn_id>#2`, `#3` and so on. A replay with a valid
`unit_cost` and `reason` returns the first request's result with
`duplicate: true` and writes nothing. The replay check runs before the
product is read and matches a movement of any type. Reusing a
receipt's `client_txn_id` answers `duplicate: true` built from that
receipt, and nothing is written. Use a `client_txn_id` that no other
movement has used.

**Accounting.** A nonzero change posts Dr Inventory asset / Cr the item's
`writedown_account_id` (or `expense_account_id` when it has none) when the
cost went up, and the reverse when it went down. No account:
`post_status: failed`, `post_error: INVENTORY_BOOKS_ACCOUNT_MISSING`. A
place with nothing on hand changes no value: `post_status: not_required`.

**Standard cost edits write the same movements.** Changing an item's
`standard_cost` (product update, `PATCH /user/inventory_item/{item_id}`)
writes a `cost_update` with reason `Estimated cost changed` for each place
valued at its estimated cost (no average, no last receipt, not written
down). Places on average or receipt cost are untouched. If the movements
cannot be written the edit is refused and nothing is saved. Routes that
`$set` fields directly (`PATCH /entity/data` `bulk_update`, automation
`update_record`, formula fields) refuse `standard_cost`
(`FIELD_NOT_EDITABLE` on bulk update).

Privilege: tenant admin, or `U` on module `inventory_item`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `INVENTORY_COST_INVALID` | `unit_cost` is missing, not a number, or negative |
| `INVENTORY_COST_UNCHANGED` | the cost is already `unit_cost` at every place in scope, or no place holds the item. `data.position_count` is how many places were looked at |
| `INVENTORY_TXN_REASON_REQUIRED` | `reason` is blank |
| `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_INVENTORY_ITEM` | the caller may not change items |
| `INVENTORY_REQUIRES_PRO` | the tenant's plan has no Inventory |
| `INVENTORY_SITE_CODE_UNKNOWN` | `site_code` is not a registered site, on a tenant with a site registry |
| `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_ID_INVALID` | `product_id` is missing or not an id |
| `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` | no such item |
| `INVENTORY_PRODUCT_LOOKUP_FAILED` | the product could not be read |
| `INVENTORY_UOM_CONVERSION_INVALID` | `uom` converts to a factor of 0 or less |
| `INVENTORY_STOCK_READ_FAILED` | the item's stock rows could not be read |
| `INVENTORY_BALANCE_UPDATE_FAILED` | the write failed; nothing recorded |
| `INVENTORY_ITEM_NOT_STOCKED` | the item is `non_stock` |
| `INVENTORY_MATRIX_PARENT_NOT_STOCKED` | the item has options; update a variant |
| `INVENTORY_UOM_UNKNOWN`, `INVENTORY_UOM_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`, `INVENTORY_PACK_SIZE_UNKNOWN` | `uom` cannot be converted to the stocking unit |
| `INVENTORY_BALANCE_BUSY` | stock kept changing while this was saved; nothing recorded, safe to retry |
| `INVENTORY_LEDGER_FAULT` | server without transactions only; see `POST /user/inventory_txn` |

unit_cost.description: The new cost per `uom`. 0 is allowed.

uom.description: Blank is the item's stocking unit. Otherwise converted like a receipt cost ($36 a case of 24 is $1.50 each).

site_code.description: Blank is every site. Otherwise that site only.

client_txn_id.description: Idempotency key for the whole request.

value_change_total.description: Signed: the sum of value_after - value_before.

duplicate.description: Present and true on a replay.

get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_txn`. Pages over movements whose `post_status` is
`pending`, `failed` or blank, oldest first.

`blocked_reason` is `READY_TO_POST` when the journal entry builds,
`NOT_REQUIRED` when no entry is owed, or the error code that stops the entry
(for example `INVENTORY_BOOKS_ACCOUNT_MISSING`). An entry that fails to build
for another reason shows `BUILD_FAILED`. A failed read answers
`INVENTORY_BOOKS_QUEUE_FAILED`.

A pending receipt against a purchase order reads `grni_account_id` from the
movement. With that account and the asset account set, it shows
`READY_TO_POST`. Without one of them it shows
`INVENTORY_BOOKS_ACCOUNT_MISSING`.

Reads every movement in the company, filtered only by
`match_filter_dict`. Site access is not checked.

parameters.description:

`post_status`, `books_entity_id`, `source_entity_type`. A value is a
string or a list of strings. Other keys, and object values, are ignored.
`post_status` narrows the queue and cannot widen it. `posted`
always returns an empty page. `pending` leaves out older rows
with no status, which the unfiltered queue shows as `pending`.

200.description:
`{result: 1, data: [{inventory_txn_id, txn_type, product_name, total_value, timestamp, post_status, blocked_reason}], total_count, page_num, page_size, count, by_reason}`.
`count` and `by_reason` cover this page. `total_count` covers every match.

get.description:
Needs `R` on `inventory_item`. Reads up to 5000 stock rows that are not `inactive`.

`stock` has value by cost basis, reorder counts (`reorder_now_count`,
`reorder_soon_count` within `horizon_days`), out-of-stock and negative
counts, perishable rows expiring within `horizon_days`, and the ten highest
values. `counts` covers the last 12 posted stocktakes. `forecast` covers
closed forecast periods. `counts` and `forecast` filter by `site_code` only
and ignore `location_code`.

If the `counts` or `forecast` read fails, the answer is still
`result: 1`. That part is then `{"error": "COUNT_QUERY_FAILED"}` or
`{"error": "FORECAST_QUERY_FAILED"}`. Check for `error` in each part.
